Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

discovery noun

also discoveries, make a discovery, a great discovery, find (something found)

classical

Cic. Mur. 61: inventa Zēnōnis (Lewis & Short)
Ov. Met. 1.521: inventum medicīna meum est

inventum, inventī n.

noun, second declension

a discovery, an invention: something found out

What has been found out or devised, a discovery and an invention alike: Zeno’s doctrines, Apollo’s medicine.

Other words

  • inventiō, inventiōnis f. — the finding out, discovering (the act or the faculty)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.61: illa vīs quae investīgat occulta, quae inventiō atque excōgitātiō dīcitur (Lewis & Short)

    In rhetoric, the finding of arguments, the first part of the art.

Examples

  • inventum medicīna meum est

    medicine is my discoveryOv. Met. 1.521

See also find, learn, new, science.
